tecnicas.observacao: Proposta do estudo: um recuperador baseado em análise estática da árvore de estrutura do repositório obtém quatro fontes de contexto (Definitions of EIF, Callers of EIF, Error Function, Callers of EF), e um compositor de prompt acrescenta assinatura e resumo das funções (gerados por LLM) e fatias de cinco linhas, combinando-os com modelos de prompt. Mecanismos listados para a condição RLCE One-shot, a única comparável aos baselines (ambos one-shot, legenda da Tabela 2): instrução Detail (papel de programador e diretriz de usar o contexto), um exemplo completo de reparo e o contexto recuperado mais a função com erro. O prompt base (Preliminary) já tem contexto (a função com erro); o RLCE acrescenta contexto de nível de repositório, da mesma categoria. O contraste RLCE contra Preliminary isola o pacote de contexto, não uma fonte de contexto específica. O RLCE também foi executado com Simple, Detail e CoT (Tabela 2).

citacoes.trecho: This paper investigates the performance of popular LLMs in handling repository-level repair tasks.
To solve the problem, we propose a simple and universal repository-level context extraction method (RLCE) designed to provide more precise context for repository-level code repair tasks.
To demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, we implement a preliminary method as the baseline that only provides the function itself where the error is located as the context.
Finally, 5 segments with the highest similarity are selected as the context.
We use two types of instructions, Simple and Detail, in the experiment.
We use the same instruction as the Detail method in the zero-shot strategy in the experiment and add a complete repair example.
To investigate the efficacy of the CoT strategy in the field of repository-level APR, we propose a straightforward zero-shot-CoT [14] approach in this paper.
Detailed descriptions of the Preliminary and Slice-similarity methods can be found in Section 4.3, both employing the one-shot prompting strategy.
citacoes.localizador: Legenda da Tabela 2, p. 7 do PDF

citacoes.trecho: In these experiments, we remove three context sources and extra semantic information, excluding EF due to the inclusion of error localization.
Furthermore, datasets created too early may pose a potential risk of data leakage if used as training data for LLMs.
To minimize the risk of leakage due to the repositories being used as training data for LLMs, we set the search date condition to later than October 1, 2021.
From the analysis above, we hypothesize that in the CoT method, incorrect interpretations can introduce significant interference, leading to erroneous outcomes.

We posit that, for program repair tasks, a longer prompt may provide more information to the large language model, but simultaneously, it may also distract the model, increasing the difficulty of repair.
Additionally, in our experiments, we standardize the temperature parameter across all LLMs to 0, ensuring stable outputs when facing the same prompt.
Increasing the temperature parameter leads to unstable model outputs, potentially influencing the final results.
Secondly, an increase in the scale and complexity of repositories may escalate the cost and difficulty of context retrieval, affecting the reliability of the results.
However, the repository-level context offered by the preliminary method often proves redundant and imprecise and easily exceeds the prompt length limit of LLMs.
In practical repair tasks, it is desirable for the model to exhibit low sensitivity to prompting strategies.

However, given that RepoBugs is the only dataset known to us specifically designed for repository-level error repair, the generalization of our approach to datasets involving other error types may vary.
Then, the two experts independently evaluated all the experimental results.
